provenance.note: Sabal palmetto (cabbage palmetto) is the drawable stand-in for Rhopalostylis sapida (nīkau), the only native palm in New Zealand and the tree Auckland's coastal and volcanic suburbs are planted with. Both are single-trunked (Monocaul) palms of the same height class with a narrow crown, so the model reads correctly; growth form, evergreen flag, height_m and crown_width_m are the stand-in model's, from schema/v0.1/flora-taxa.json, so placement matches what is drawn. native_status follows the Wikipedia article, which records the nīkau as endemic to New Zealand. community_weight is judgement: a relative share of 1.0 among the garden's trees, divided by the importer's 1.0 multiplier for Native plants.

provenance.note: Washingtonia filifera (California fan palm) is the drawable stand-in for Phoenix canariensis (Canary Island date palm), an ornamental planted along Auckland's suburban frontages. Both are single-trunked (Monocaul) palms of the same height class; the Washingtonia model is the only other palm of this build in flora-taxa.json that is not itself a tropical American species, and its stiffer fan of leaves reads correctly against the date palm's heavier drooping crown. Growth form, evergreen flag, height_m and crown_width_m are the model's, so placement matches what is drawn. native_status is Introduced: the Canary Island date palm is a native of the Canary Islands, not of New Zealand. community_weight is judgement: a relative share of 1.0 among the garden's trees, divided by the importer's 0.3 multiplier for Introduced plants.

provenance.note: Magnolia grandiflora (southern magnolia) is the drawable stand-in for Metrosideros excelsa (pōhutukawa), the broad-leaved evergreen tree New Zealanders plant for its red flowers. Both are wide-crowned evergreen (Decurrent) trees with simple entire leathery leaves, so the model reads correctly, though the magnolia's crown is broader and its leaves far larger than the pōhutukawa's. Growth form, evergreen flag, height_m and crown_width_m are the model's, so placement matches what is drawn. native_status follows the Wikipedia article, which records the pōhutukawa as endemic to New Zealand. community_weight is judgement: a relative share of 0.6 among the garden's trees, and the only wide-crowned tree here given any real weight, since a 20 m crown fills a small plot on its own. Divided by the importer's 1.0 multiplier for Native plants.

provenance.note: Ilex opaca (American holly) is the drawable stand-in for Griselinia littoralis (broadleaf), the glossy-leaved coastal evergreen New Zealanders use for almost every hedge. Both are broad-leaved evergreens that hold a dense, wind-tolerant hedge; the holly is spiny and the broadleaf's leaves are larger and rounder, which the model does not capture. Growth form, evergreen flag, height_m and crown_width_m are the model's, so placement matches what is drawn. native_status follows the Wikipedia article, which records the broadleaf as endemic to New Zealand. community_weight is judgement: the largest share of any entry here, 2.0, because an Auckland hedge is usually several metres of this plant, against a 1.0 multiplier for Native plants.

provenance.note: Pinus strobus (eastern white pine) is the drawable stand-in for Dacrycarpus dacrydioides (kahikatea), the tall podocarp that survives in Auckland's older gardens and on volcanic ground. Both are single-trunked (Excurrent) conifers with a whorled crown reaching the same height class; the pine's needles and cones are unlike the kahikatea's small scale leaves and fleshy seed, which the model does not capture. Growth form, evergreen flag, height_m and crown_width_m are the model's, so placement matches what is drawn. native_status follows the Wikipedia article, which records the kahikatea as endemic to New Zealand. community_weight is judgement: a relative share of 0.5 among the garden's trees, kept low because a 30 m conifer with a 15 m crown overfills a small plot. Divided by the importer's 1.0 multiplier for Native plants.

provenance.note: Yucca rostrata (beaked yucca) is the drawable stand-in for Phormium tenax (harakeke, New Zealand flax). Both are rosettes of stiff, sword-shaped, evergreen leaves a few metres tall with no woody trunk, so the model reads correctly; the yucca's leaves are narrower, paler and far more rigid than the flax's arching green fans. Growth form, evergreen flag, height_m and crown_width_m are the model's, so placement matches what is drawn. native_status follows the Wikipedia article, which records the harakeke as endemic to New Zealand and a staple of Māori weaving. community_weight is judgement: a relative share of 1.0, because flax is planted in clumps along a New Zealand garden's edges. Divided by the importer's 1.0 multiplier for Native plants.

provenance.note: Quercus alba (white oak) is the drawable stand-in for Quercus robur (English oak), a planted shade tree of Auckland's older European-influenced gardens. Both are spreading (Decurrent) oaks of the same height class; the white oak's crown is narrower and its leaves deeply lobed, while the English oak's are smaller and pinnate-lobed. Growth form, evergreen flag, height_m and crown_width_m are the model's, so placement matches what is drawn. native_status is Introduced: the English oak is a native of Europe. community_weight is judgement: a relative share of 1.0, divided by the importer's 0.3 multiplier for Introduced plants.

provenance.note: Taxus canadensis (Canada yew) is the drawable stand-in for Buxus sempervirens (common box), the low evergreen hedging plant still clipped along New Zealand garden paths. Both are small, dense, evergreen conifer-family plants, so the model reads correctly; the yew is a sprawling ground-level shrub where the box is a clipped upright hedge, so this is the loosest match in the catalog and is recorded at Low confidence for that reason. Growth form, evergreen flag, height_m and crown_width_m are the model's, so placement matches what is drawn. native_status is Introduced, box being a native of western Europe and North Africa. community_weight is judgement: a relative share of 0.3, a short run of path edging rather than a boundary hedge. Divided by the importer's 0.3 multiplier for Introduced plants.
